adjudication.rationale: Diff shows GoogleCalendarService.createEvent now selects the target calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and then falls back to `"primary"` when no match (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination calendar entry has no `credentialId`, it creates events for *all* credentials matching `destination.integration` (`destinationCalendarCredentials.map(...createEvent(c, event))`) without providing any externalId mapping. Since those destination entries also lack `credentialId`, GoogleCalendarService's `find` returns nothing for each credential, so each credential inserts into its own `primary` calendar (silent wrong-calendar + potential duplicates). Additionally, CalendarManager.createEvent returns `externalId` from the caller parameter regardless of whether the service actually used it (or fell back to primary), so downstream code that uses `result.externalId` for `externalCalendarId` can persist undefined/mismatched values.
